interval_years.quote: All licenses issued under this chapter shall be renewed every two years in accordance with RSA 310:8.

required.quote: All optometrists licensed in this state shall be required to take annual courses of study in subjects relating to the practice of the profession of optometry.

hours_per_period.quote: The length of study shall be prescribed by the board, with a minimum of 15 hours in a calendar year.

period_years.quote: a minimum of 15 hours in a calendar year

value: subjects relating to the practice of the profession of optometry
pharmacology and ocular disease (minimum 50 hours/year for pharmaceutical certification, minimum 20 hours in formal courses)
glaucoma-specific education (minimum 10 hours for glaucoma-certified optometrists, minimum 7 hours formal)
topical_requirements.quote: An optometrist certified to use pharmaceutical agents in the practice of optometry shall complete a minimum of 50 hours of continuing education every year in order to maintain pharmaceutical certification. A minimum of 20 hours shall be by participation in formal courses and the remainder by independent study.

available.quote: All boards or commissions shall grant a license to an individual certified or licensed in another state if it determines that the requirements or standards for certification or licensure in that state are equivalent to, or greater than, those established in New Hampshire.

requirements.value: Reciprocal licensure available if the other state's requirements are equivalent to or greater than New Hampshire's. Board posts list of qualifying states. Temporary license (120 days) available pending full review.
requirements.quote: All boards or commissions shall grant a license to an individual certified or licensed in another state if it determines that the requirements or standards for certification or licensure in that state are equivalent to, or greater than, those established in New Hampshire.

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of a felony or any offense involving moral turpitude

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Unfitness or incompetency by reason of negligent habits or other causes; or negligent or willful acts performed in a manner inconsistent with the health or safety of persons under the care of the licensee

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Addiction to the use of alcohol or other habit-forming drugs to a degree which renders him unfit to practice under this chapter

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Suspension or revocation of a license, similar to one issued under this chapter, in another jurisdiction and not reinstated

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of any pharmaceutical agent not authorized under RSA 327:6-a or outside the defined formulary
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The use of any pharmaceutical agent by an optometrist not authorized under RSA 327:6-a or the use of any pharmaceutical agent other than those agents described in RSA 327:1 or those previously approved by the joint credentialing committee

insurance_required.quote: Have at least $1,000,000 of professional liability insurance coverage.

definition_quote.value: "Practice of optometry" means the employment of any methods or means, other than surgery, for the diagnosis and treatment of any optical defect, deficiency, deformity, or disease of the human eye, adnexa and eyelids; diagnosis and treatment of any visual or muscular anomaly of the visual system; adaptation or prescribing of spectacle lenses, contact lenses, prisms or ocular exercises; prescribing, administering or dispensing of pharmaceutical agents; application, prescribing, or removal of FDA approved medical devices; and diagnosis of acute angle closure glaucoma.
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of optometry" means the employment of any methods or means, other than surgery, for the: (a) Diagnosis and treatment of any optical defect, deficiency, deformity, or disease of the human eye, adnexa and eyelids.

value: diagnosis and treatment of optical defects, deficiencies, deformities, or diseases of the human eye, adnexa and eyelids
diagnosis and treatment of visual or muscular anomalies of the visual system
adaptation or prescribing of spectacle lenses, contact lenses, prisms or ocular exercises
prescribing, administering or dispensing of pharmaceutical agents
application, prescribing, or removal of FDA approved medical devices including contact lenses, plano lenses, and punctal plugs
diagnosis of acute angle closure glaucoma and emergency care
methods_authorized.quote: "Practice of optometry" means the employment of any methods or means, other than surgery, for the: (a) Diagnosis and treatment of any optical defect, deficiency, deformity, or disease of the human eye, adnexa and eyelids. (b) Diagnosis and treatment of any visual or muscular anomaly of the visual system. (c) Adaptation or prescribing of spectacle lenses, contact lenses, prisms or ocular exercises for the correction, relief or aid of the visual functions. (d) Prescribing, administering or dispensing of pharmaceutical agents. (e) Application, prescribing, or removal of Food and Drug Administration approved medical devices

drug_authority.value: Licensed optometrists authorized under RSA 327:6-a may prescribe, administer, and dispense a broad formulary of pharmaceutical agents including topical and oral antibiotics, anti-allergy agents, anesthetics, ocular lubricants, orally administered analgesics (including class III and IV controlled substances), anti-glaucoma agents (with glaucoma certification), corticosteroids, antivirals, and vaccines. Schedule I and II controlled substances are prohibited.
drug_authority.quote: administer, prescribe or dispense any pharmaceutical product designated as a schedule I or schedule II controlled substance under RSA 318-B:1-a

surgery_prohibited.quote: "Practice of optometry" means the employment of any methods or means, other than surgery

surgery_definition.value: Any procedure in which human tissue is cut, altered, or otherwise infiltrated by mechanical means, including use of lasers for therapeutic and photorefractive purposes, ionizing radiation, therapeutic ultrasound, or medication administered by injection
surgery_definition.quote: "Surgery" means any procedure in which human tissue is cut, altered, or otherwise infiltrated by mechanical means. Surgical procedures shall include the use of lasers for therapeutic and photorefractive purposes, ionizing radiation, therapeutic ultrasound, or medication administered by injection

foreign_body_removal_authorized.quote: provided that the removal of superficial foreign bodies from the eye, adnexa or eyelid shall not be considered a surgical procedure prohibited by this chapter

value: removal of superficial foreign bodies from the eye, adnexa or eyelid (not deeper than corneal epithelium within 3mm of visual axis)
minor_surgical_procedures_authorized.quote: the removal of superficial foreign bodies from the eye, adnexa or eyelid shall not be considered a surgical procedure prohibited by this chapter. With respect to a foreign body, any part of which is situated within 3 millimeters of the visual axis, "superficial foreign body" means that which has not penetrated deeper than the corneal epithelium.

glaucoma_treatment_authorized.quote: Anti-glaucoma agents provided that an optometrist may dispense or prescribe such agents if the optometrist has met the requirements of RSA 327:6-c.

anaphylaxis_treatment_authorized.quote: Diphenhydramine, epinephrine, or an equivalent medication administered by injection or other administration route to counter anaphylaxis or anaphylactic reaction.

vision_therapy_authorized.quote: Adaptation or prescribing of spectacle lenses, contact lenses, prisms or ocular exercises for the correction, relief or aid of the visual functions.

immunization_authority.quote: Influenza, COVID-19, and shingles vaccines which have been approved by the Food and Drug Administration to adults.

value: Schedule III and IV controlled substances permitted as orally administered analgesics when approved pursuant to RSA 327:6-a, VI and included in formulary
controlled_substance_schedule_restrictio.quote: administer, prescribe or dispense any pharmaceutical product designated as a schedule I or schedule II controlled substance under RSA 318-B:1-a

oral_pharmaceutical_authority.quote: Orally administered analgesic agents used for the purpose of alleviating pain caused by a disease or abnormal condition of the human eye or eyelid, or structures posterior to the iris.

pharmaceutical_certification_required.quote: Only licensed optometrists who have successfully completed examinations on pharmacological substances and other treatments of diseases of the eye, adnexa and eyelids, who have met acceptable standards of education and professional competence as determined by the board, and who hold current certification in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), shall be authorized to use pharmaceutical agents in the practice of optometry.

value: TPA/G certified optometrist (TPA plus glaucoma treatment)
tiered_license_types.quote: Upon certification to treat glaucoma patients pursuant to RSA 327:6-c, the office shall issue a license to the optometrist with a "tpa/g" certification.

specialty_certification_types.quote: Upon certification to treat glaucoma patients pursuant to RSA 327:6-c, the office shall issue a license to the optometrist with a "tpa/g" certification.

pharmacology_training_hours_required.quote: an approved course shall be given by an accredited school or college of optometry in the United States and shall consist of a minimum of 105 hours, of which a minimum of 25 hours shall be in direct clinical training

supervised_clinical_internship_required.quote: a minimum of 105 hours, of which a minimum of 25 hours shall be in direct clinical training

referral_to_physician_required.quote: Upon such diagnosis, an optometrist may administer emergency care and shall immediately refer the patient to an ophthalmologist.

comanagement_with_ophthalmologist_requir.quote: therapeutic pharmaceutical agent certified optometrists are required to provide evidence of successful collaborative treatment and co-management of 25 glaucoma patients

telemedicine_authorized.quote: Persons licensed by the office of professional licensure and certification shall be permitted to provide services through the use of telemedicine, as defined in RSA 310:7.

contact_lens_prescription_expiration_yea.quote: Unless otherwise specified by the prescriber for health reasons, a contact lens prescription shall expire one year from the date of issue.
